newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: SQUASH-JANSHER EASES INTO SHOWDOWN WITH EYLES.
newsitem.headline: SQUASH-JANSHER EASES INTO SHOWDOWN WITH EYLES.

text.p: Jansher Khan eased into the
final of the World Open on Thursday with a 15-9 15-9 15-8
victory over fourth seed Peter Nicol fof Scotland.
The match extended the Pakistani further than any other in
the tournament so far, but should still have left him relatively
fresh for the final on Friday when he defends the title he has
already won a record seven times.
In contrast, his opponent in the final, second seed Rodney
Eyles of Australia, had to get out of jail for the second
successive day to beat Chris Walker of England 15-12 15-7 14-15
4-15 15-14 in 73 tension-packed minutes.
In the quarter-finals Eyles had escaped from two games down
and 10-12 in the third against Zubair Jahan of Pakistan.
"I actually played my best squash of the tournament against
Chris in the first two games," Eyles said. "Then when I was 5-0
up in the third, I committed the cardinal sin. I started
thinking about tomorrow.
"I have been in this game long enough to know nothing is
over until your are back in the changing room. But I have never
made the World Open final before and I guess it just crept into
my mind when I looked secure for a win.
"By the time I got my mind back on the job, Chris was
jumping about all over the court."
Eyles returned to his solid rallying in the fifth and led
5-1 and 10-8. But Walker unleashed a stream of inventive shots,
often from extreme recovery positions to overtake to 12-10 and
then to 14-12.
The point for 14-12 saw the Australian hit a long angled
drop shot that would have been a winner against a less mobile
oponent. But Walker managed a spread-eagled recovery shot and
Eyles'sreply struck the tin.
Eyles then hit a calm backhand drop and a sweet forehand
straight nick before clinching his place in the final with a
backhand after Walker had called for a risky one point
tie-break.
